question_en:
My grandmother left behind a small bronze horse and an old note with writing on it. I want to clarify their origin. Please answer the following questions:
1. What are the artist and model name of the small bronze horse, respectively?
2. Based on the record for this particular object and the artist's birth and death years, determine whether this piece was cast during the artist's lifetime or after their death.
3. Read the text on the note and determine whether it refers to the horse depicted in this work, or to another work by this artist and another racehorse. If it is the latter, please provide the name of the other work and the name of the corresponding racehorse.

Answer format: Please answer in separate points numbered (1)–(3). Each point should only answer the corresponding sub-question and provide all information required by that question.
answer:
(1) Artist: Pierre-Jules Mêne; Model: Ibrahim - Cheval Arabe Ramené d’Egypte no. 2 (Cheval arabe (Ibrahim) n°2).

(2) Cast after the artist's death.

(3) Text on the note: Jockey vainqueur; more likely refers to another work by the artist, Jockey à cheval (also known as Vainqueur du Derby), corresponding to the racehorse Caractacus.

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 8-2-A01

## Step 01 · Decompose the question and establish fields to verify

**Action:** Record required fields for each sub-question according to the current prompt; first identify the bridge entity from the input image, then map each answer field to a verifiable source.

**Evidence Observation:**

My grandmother left behind a small bronze horse and an old note with writing on it. I want to clarify their origin. Please answer the following questions:
1. What are the artist and model name of the small bronze horse, respectively?
2. Based on the record for this particular object and the artist's birth and death years, determine whether this piece was cast during the artist's lifetime or after their death.
3. Read the text on the note and determine whether it refers to the horse depicted in this work, or to another work by this artist and another racehorse. If it is the latter, please provide the name of the other work and the name of the corresponding racehorse.

Answer format: Please answer in separate points numbered (1)–(3). Each point should only answer the corresponding sub-question and provide all information required by that question.

**Evidence Links:**

Current prompt and input attachments; this step introduces no external web pages.

**Result of this step:** The retrieval path expands according to these sub-questions; the image serves as the entry point for the object, while numbering, dates, statistics, and status must be read from corresponding records.

## Step 02 · Read two clues: the bronze horse and the note

**Action:** Record the subject form and legible text separately, then decide on search terms.

**Evidence Observation:**

The bronze horse is a standing horse without a rider; the text on the note reads "Jockey vainqueur," and the final period does not affect reading. First establish two fields to verify: "object identity" and "story told by the note." Do not assume they share the same source merely because they are placed together.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.sillafineantiques.com/ibrahim-arabian-stallion-pierre-jules-mene/

**Result of this step:** Use French animal sculpture bronze horses as the retrieval entry point for the object; keep the note separate for now.

## Step 03 · Establish model candidates

**Action:** Example query: bronze Arabian stallion oval base Pierre Jules Mene Ibrahim no 2; compare item photos and names from Silla one by one.

**Evidence Observation:**

A professional antique dealer page is titled "Ibrahim - Arabian Stallion," with the artist field listed as Pierre-Jules Mêne; the full name of the corresponding model is "Ibrahim - Cheval Arabe Ramené d'Egypte no. 2." The matching basis is the configuration of the entire horse and base; one cannot specify the foundry based on base marks invisible in edited images.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.sillafineantiques.com/ibrahim-arabian-stallion-pierre-jules-mene/

**Result of this step:** Lock in the artist and model; the next step is to read the casting date of this particular object.

## Step 04 · Distinguish between model creation time and casting time

**Action:** On the same object page, search for three types of fields: model, cast, and posthumous.

**Evidence Observation:**

The record places the model creation in 1843, but lists this specific piece as "cast circa 1880" and explicitly states "posthumous casting." The year of the original model cannot be directly used as the manufacturing year for every subsequent bronze cast of it.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.sillafineantiques.com/ibrahim-arabian-stallion-pierre-jules-mene/

**Result of this step:** Use circa 1880, not 1843, for the second question.

## Step 05 · Verify posthumous casting judgment using independent artist records

**Action:** Precisely search the author field in the Reims museum collection by name, then compare the artist's death year with the casting date.

**Evidence Observation:**

Reims gives 1810–1879. Circa 1880 is later than 1879, consistent with the object record's wording of posthumous casting; one can only determine the category of during-lifetime vs. posthumous, and cannot infer from a difference of about one year that the artist personally participated in the casting or that it came from a specific workshop.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.sillafineantiques.com/ibrahim-arabian-stallion-pierre-jules-mene/
https://musees-reims.fr/oeuvre/vainqueur-de-la-course

**Result of this step:** Form an evidence combination of "artist death year 1879 + cast circa 1880 = posthumous casting."

## Step 06 · Check the current model against the semantic meaning of the note

**Action:** Example query: Pierre-Jules Mêne jockey vainqueur sculpture; first compare the textual meaning with the visual composition.

**Evidence Observation:**

"Jockey" means jockey, and "vainqueur" means winner; the current model features only a horse, with no jockey appearing. This mismatch is not proof that the note was historically misplaced, but it is sufficient to require continuing the search for another equestrian work by the same artist.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.sillafineantiques.com/ibrahim-arabian-stallion-pierre-jules-mene/
https://musees-reims.fr/oeuvre/vainqueur-de-la-course

**Result of this step:** Retain the artist, but expand the object search using "jockey" and "vainqueur."

## Step 07 · Find another work featuring a rider

**Action:** Access the Reims museum collection record for "vainqueur-de-la-course" and read the title, artist, material, and date.

**Evidence Observation:**

The museum title relationships connect "Jockey à cheval," "Vainqueur du Derby," and "Vainqueur de la course." The work is an original wax model from circa 1863, depicting a jockey on a horse; the artist remains Mêne, so both the figure composition and the semantic meaning of the note align better with this than with "Ibrahim."

**Evidence Links:**

https://musees-reims.fr/oeuvre/vainqueur-de-la-course

**Result of this step:** Obtain the next work title: "Vainqueur du Derby."

## Step 08 · Trace from the work title to the racehorse explanation

**Action:** Example query: Mêne Vainqueur du Derby Caractacus; read the work description in Christie's lot 4913216 rather than taking only the title.

**Evidence Observation:**

The lot essay states that this work "is considered to depict" Caractacus, the 1862 Derby champion; the sequence of an 1863 Salon wax model and an 1864 bronze edition aligns with the date of the original Reims model. Here, retain the strength of the attribution inference; do not write the work explanation as if the horse's name were independently provable from the photograph.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.christies.com/lot/lot-4913216

**Result of this step:** Obtain two cross-verifiable fields: "Caractacus" and "1862 Epsom Derby."

## Step 09 · Verify the race year and champion

**Action:** Locate 1862 in The Jockey Club's "Epsom Derby Previous Winners" table.

**Evidence Observation:**

The official list of past champions matches 1862 with Caractacus, supporting the race result portion of the auction description. However, the race result table cannot prove which sculpture the note historically accompanied, nor can it rename "Caractacus" as "Ibrahim."

**Evidence Links:**

https://int.thejockeyclub.co.uk/epsom-derby/about-the-event/previous-winners/

**Result of this step:** The usual interpretation of the other work is supported by independent race records.

## Step 10 · Address competing narratives on commercial object pages

**Action:** Regarding Silla's claim of "French Derby winner," use an example query: France Galop 1843 Prix du Jockey Club Renonce.

**Evidence Observation:**

France Galop explains "Prix du Jockey Club" as the French Derby and records that in 1843, Renonce defeated Prospero in a rerun; this conflicts with commercial copy that writes "Ibrahim" as the champion of that year. The object page can be used to identify this bronze horse, but it is not the final evidence for this racing history.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.sillafineantiques.com/ibrahim-arabian-stallion-pierre-jules-mene/
https://www.france-galop.com/en/content/jockey-club-history-other-derby

**Result of this step:** Exclude the sideline that forcibly interprets the note as a story of Ibrahim winning the championship.

## Step 11 · Use contemporary newspapers and author metadata for final disambiguation

**Action:** Compare the digital text of L'Illustration from May 27, 1843, and re-examine the artist's birth and death years in the auction title.

**Evidence Observation:**

Contemporary reports also connect the Jockey-Club prize with Renonce. The Christie's title lists the artist's death year as 1871, which conflicts with official artist data; adopt Reims' 1810–1879 for birth and death years. Do not erase its independent cross-referenced work description due to this title error.

**Evidence Links:**

https://readingroo.ms/3/6/8/6/36868/36868-h/36868-h.htm
https://musees-reims.fr/oeuvre/vainqueur-de-la-course
https://www.christies.com/lot/lot-4913216

**Result of this step:** Separately determine adoptable fields, erroneous fields, and inference boundaries.

## Step 12 · Consolidate item by item without establishing false provenance

**Action:** Establish a three-question checklist: artist and model; casting time of this piece; reading of the note, the other work, and the horse name.

**Evidence Observation:**

The first question is supported by the Silla object page; the second by circa 1880 and the death year 1879; the third by the semantic meaning of the note, the rider composition in Reims, the Christie's explanation, and official race results jointly. There are yet no certificates, old collection inventories, or historical note records proving true co-provenance.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.sillafineantiques.com/ibrahim-arabian-stallion-pierre-jules-mene/
https://musees-reims.fr/oeuvre/vainqueur-de-la-course
https://www.christies.com/lot/lot-4913216
https://int.thejockeyclub.co.uk/epsom-derby/about-the-event/previous-winners/

**Result of this step:** Finally use the qualifying phrase "more likely corresponds to another work."

## Step 13 · Check evidence dependencies and answer boundaries

**Action:** Connect the obtained bridge entities in order of dependency, and check each question for mismatches in numbering, changes in time conventions, or inferences written as facts.

**Evidence Observation:**

Dependency chain: bronze horse without rider → "Ibrahim n°2" object record → circa 1880 and death year 1879; note → same-artist work with rider → Caractacus → official race results.

Boundaries to retain: the true attribution of the note is unproven; the antique dealer's champion claim conflicts with official history; the Christie's title contains an error in the death year.

**Evidence Links:**

Current prompt and input attachments; this step introduces no external web pages.

**Result of this step:** Each field uses the evidence directly corresponding to it above; organize the confirmed conclusions according to the question's specified numbering, table format, and units.

## Step 14 · final_answer

**Action:** Submit the answer with the fields required by the current question.

**Evidence observation:** Cross-checking of the object, source, and corresponding version has been completed; previously unconfirmable information is retained.

**Result of this step:**

(1) Artist: Pierre-Jules Mêne; Model: Ibrahim - Cheval Arabe Ramené d'Egypte no. 2 (Cheval arabe (Ibrahim) n°2).

(2) Cast after the artist's death.

(3) Text on the note: Jockey vainqueur; more likely refers to another work by the artist, Jockey à cheval (also known as Vainqueur du Derby), corresponding to the racehorse Caractacus.
